# Test fixtures

## Real QVD files (`real/`)

These are genuine QlikView-written QVD files, used to validate the decoder
against real QlikView output rather than against this project's own encoder.

| File | Source | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `products.qvd` | QlikView build 11282 (2012), from `qvd-reader` | 77 rows, 9 columns |
| `products.expected.csv` | CSV produced by the Java `QvdReader` from `products.qvd` | reference values |
| `wide-sparse.qvd` | from `qvd-writer` | 120 rows, 19 columns |

`products.qvd` is a good stress case: its fields are **not** stored in
bit-offset order (0, 53, 8, ...), and `Listenpreis` genuinely mixes 25 integer
and 35 double symbols in one column, exercising `--numeric-promote`.

`wide-sparse.qvd` covers columns whose symbol table is empty (which must decode
as all-null, not as zeros), `UNKNOWN` declared types, and field names starting
with `#`.

`TestRealQVDProducts` converts `products.qvd` and compares **every cell**
against `products.expected.csv`, joining on `ProduktNr` because physical row
order is not preserved. Numeric columns are compared after normalizing the
Java reader's German decimal comma.

## Synthetic fixtures

`sample-small.qvd` (1000 rows) is generated by `internal/qvdtest/cmd/genfixture`
and covers every resolved output type: `INTEGER`, `ASCII`, `MONEY` (exact
decimal, comma decimal separator), `DATE`, `REAL` with nulls, `TIMESTAMP` and
`TIME`. Real QVDs rarely contain all of these in one table, so this fixture
fills the gaps the real files leave.

Unit tests also build synthetic QVDs in memory at run time via
`internal/qvdtest`, so no setup is needed:

```sh
go test ./...
```

To write a larger fixture for benchmarking (not committed, it is regenerable):

```sh
go run ./internal/qvdtest/cmd/genfixture testdata/sample-large.qvd 1000000
```

## Your own fixtures

Point `QVD2PARQUET_TESTDATA` at a directory of `.qvd` files to run the
converter against them:

```sh
QVD2PARQUET_TESTDATA=/path/to/qvds go test ./internal/convert -run TestRealFixtures -v
```

For each file the test converts with `--quality-gate=full`, checks that source
and Parquet row counts and fingerprints agree, writes and re-reads a schema
report, and re-runs with `--workers=1` to confirm the content fingerprints
match. A column that fails the default `--mixed=error` policy is not treated as
a converter bug; the test retries that fixture with `--mixed=string`.

## Recommended fixture sizes

| Fixture | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| small (< 10k rows) | correctness, fast iteration |
| medium (~1M rows) | developer iteration, quality gate cost |
| large (> 50M rows) | throughput and peak memory |
| high-cardinality strings | symbol table memory, dictionary encoding |
| wide table (100+ columns) | per-column overhead |
| mixed-type / dual-heavy | type policy behaviour |
